children: Shop inflation in the U.K. jumped to its highest level in over two years as rising energy, input, and raw-material costs start to push up prices, according to data from the British Retail Consortium and Nielsen IQ. "The months ahead look challenging for households, with rising bills putting further pressure on budgets," BRC's Helen Dickinson says. Shop price inflation rose to 1.5% from Aug. 1 to Aug. 7 compared with the same period a year earlier, BRC and NIQ say. The figure compares with growth of 0.9% in July, according to the report. "Pressures are continuing to build across supply chains, and we can expect price competition to intensify as we move into the autumn months," NIQ's Mike Watkins says. (andrea.figueras@wsj.com)
